title: Kenton, the unbuilt music school and why it's too late
summary: Herman pressed Kenton to open a Southern California music school, but both stayed in the outer world, and it is too late now.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: I do, yeah, and I always have. Once that Kenton made me aware of why it's as important as it is. And, of course, the thing that I tried to encourage Stan to do many years ago, and it was along the same lines, basically, except it would be more of our very own production, and that was
to open a music school in Southern California. And he never entered into the spirit of that, because he felt that we could both do more out in the outer world.
And so we both remained in the outer --
But what do you think about that now?
Well, I think it's too late in my case, and probably the same with him.

And it's like everything else, probably even more so. The dedication must be complete. I know that I wouldn't be able to do what I -- any of what I'm doing now and be involved in that. For that reason along, I --
So you'd never consider then forsaking the band to move into that kind of an enterprise.
Not that kind of thing at this late date. I just don't feel that I have enough time to offer. Or would have.
